answer: A flywheel bank stores energy as motion, and an identity can rest on a signed log of spin cycles: each charge spins the rotor up, each discharge lets it coast down, and the recovered watt-hours are metered per cycle. The orchard-side flywheel spins up overnight, the wander of its speed curve is unique to its bearings, and the tide of charge and discharge follows the grid's daily rhythm. Only the flywheel that ran those cycles can present the matching log.
